newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: IGNALINA TO SIGN DEAL WITH JAPAN'S PESCO.
newsitem.headline: IGNALINA TO SIGN DEAL WITH JAPAN'S PESCO.

text.p: The Ignalina nuclear power plant will sign an agreement on Tuesday with Japan's PESCO company to suppy it with computer and oxide measuring equipment, an economy ministry official said.
The Japanese government will donate between $5 million and $6 million to the project over the next three years, Jonas Kazlauskas, an adviser to the economy minister, told Reuters.
The money will be used to set up a common data base for the entire plant to replace the system of separate data bases for each reactor, Kazlauskas said.
The agreement also provides equipment to measure oxide corrosion in the fuel channels at the plant.
The Ignalina plant consists of two units, which were commissioned in December 1983 and August 1987. The plant is expected to be decommissioned early next century.

Ignalina's two Chernobyl-style RBMK reactors are the largest of their kind and a source of constant concern for Lithuania's Scandinavian neighbours and Western European countries worried about the plant's safety.
